title: People who help us

parent.learn: Helpers and their jobs: doctor, teacher, farmer, police officer, firefighter, postman, driver.
parent.why: Knowing who does what tells the child whom to go to for help, and that many people work so we can have food, safety and school.

parent.learn: Where they work: doctor–hospital, teacher–school, farmer–field.
parent.why: Linking a job with a place helps the child understand their town and neighbourhood.

parent.learn: If lost, ask a police officer or a shopkeeper — and know a parent's phone number.
parent.why: These are safe grown-ups in a known place. India's emergency number is 112.

ask: Who helps us when we are ill?
Who brings letters and parcels to our home?
What would you like to be when you grow up? What will you do?
If you get lost in a shop, whom will you ask for help?
Can you say Mummy's or Papa's phone number?

rounds.h: A teacher helps us learn at school.

rounds.t: Who helps us when we are ill?
rounds.h: A doctor checks us and gives medicine.
Farmers grow rice, wheat, fruits and vegetables.
Firefighters use water to put out fires.

rounds.t: Who brings letters to our home?
rounds.h: The postman delivers letters and parcels.
A driver drives buses, cars and trucks.

rounds.t: Who makes tables and chairs from wood?
Who keeps us safe and helps on the roads?
rounds.h: The police keep us safe and control traffic.
A tailor sews clothes with a needle or sewing machine.
A cobbler repairs shoes and sandals.
Doctors work in hospitals and clinics.

rounds.t: If you get lost in a market, whom should you ask for help?
rounds.h: A police officer is a safe grown-up whose job is to help.
